paper_title: On White-Box Learning and Public-Key Encryption
classifications: Theory of computation → Computational complexity and cryptography
statement: We leave as an intriguing open problem the question of whether white-box learning of polynomial, or even logarithmic-degree polynomials, also can be collapsed down to the case of constant-degree functions (and thus to linear functions); if this were possible, it would show that PKE, in essence, inherently requires the structure of the LWE problem.
context: Open Problems We leave as an intriguing open problem the question of whether white-box learning of polynomial, or even logarithmic-degree polynomials, also can be collapsed down to the case of constant-degree functions (and thus to linear functions); if this were possible, it would show that PKE, in essence, inherently requires the structure of the LWE problem. Additionally, as discussed above, even when just restricting attention to learning linear functions, our learning problem generalizes LWE. It would appear that despite this, cryptographic applications of LWE (e.g., to obtain fully homomorphic encryption [14, 10]) nevertheless may still be possible from this generalized version; we leave an exploration of this for future work. 8
